critic.verdict: Still sets the bar for soundbars in 2026; the same superb Dolby Atmos performance as its predecessor, and a design refresh is overdue
Reproduced a Dolby Atmos 9.1.6 test sequence with excellent positioning; the best image positioning of the bars tested
Good value at GBP 1,449; the rear speakers manage surprising bass for their size, the build feels less premium than the 2024 Q990D
The compact dual-driver subwoofer gives controlled, meaty bass but will not replace a large standalone sub; premium price, remote has no backlight

user_sentiment.summary: Owners report a quick setup and a genuinely enveloping bubble of sound from the four-piece set; the recurring complaint is the price and that the design has not moved in three generations.

pros: 23 speakers in a 11.1.4 layout: height from the bar and from the rears
Wireless sub and wireless rears in the box, nothing to cable
Two HDMI inputs, so a console can sit behind the bar
Sound Elevation helps dialogue on 85-inch and larger TVs
cons: Most expensive bar on this list at list price
Subwoofer is compact rather than deep
Barely changed from the Q990F, which is often much cheaper
cinema_verdict: The reference four-piece Atmos system: real height channels front and back, no speaker cables anywhere, and the best object placement reviewers have measured in a soundbar.
notes: No single outlet publishes a numeric score for this model, so review_score is a synthesis of four written verdicts rather than a measured figure; confidence is medium for that reason. Peak-power and driver counts come from the reviews, not from a lab.

critic.verdict: Samsung's Dolby Atmos-in-a-box system returns with a serious boost to bass
The flagship 11.1.4 formula, with the subwoofer the biggest step on from the Q990D

user_sentiment.summary: Widely treated as the sweet spot of the range now that the Q990H is out: the same layout at a lower street price.

pros: Same 11.1.4 four-piece layout as the 2026 flagship
Bass improved over the 2024 Q990D
Two HDMI inputs
cons: Superseded, so stock is uneven across shops
Rears need a mains socket each
cinema_verdict: The Q990H's performance for less money while shops clear it: watch this one and the H together and buy whichever is cheaper.
notes: review_score mirrors the Q990H because the two reviewed almost identically; it is an editorial synthesis, not a published score.

critic.verdict: Named best soundbar under GBP 1,000 for 2026; two up-firing channels among the nine in the bar
Strong all-in-one, but HDMI passthrough is limited to 4K/60

user_sentiment.summary: Bought by people who do not want a subwoofer box in the room; owners accept less low bass in exchange.

pros: 13 speakers and two real up-firing channels in one bar
Four built-in woofers, so no subwoofer box to place
Convertible Fit and SpaceFit Sound Pro calibration
cons: No subwoofer and no rear speakers, in the box or as a matched kit
HDMI passthrough caps at 4K/60, below what a 2026 TV and console expect
cinema_verdict: The one-box answer: true height channels and no cables at all, at the cost of the bass and the surround that a four-piece set gives you.
notes: Confidence is low: the model is new and the write-ups available are short. The 4K/60 passthrough limit is recorded as a fit penalty.

critic.verdict: Recommending this is a no-brainer: dialogue, bass and Dolby Atmos all land
One step forward, two steps back; no way to tweak the Bar 7's tuning
A strong option, with AI dialogue control when paired with a compatible BRAVIA TV

user_sentiment.summary: Praised for dialogue clarity with Sony TVs; the missing EQ control is the complaint that comes up most.

pros: Two up-firing drivers at a price where they used to be absent
360 Spatial Sound Mapping places phantom speakers convincingly
One HDMI 2.1 input plus eARC
cons: No EQ adjustment at all
Subwoofer and rears are extra, which lifts the real price well above the bar's
cinema_verdict: Sony's mid-tier with real height drivers; best bought as the kit with the Sub 7, which is how the Cypriot shops list it.
notes: Reviews disagree on whether to call it 5.0.2 or 5.1.2 - the difference is whether the subwoofer is counted. The bar alone is 5.0.2.

critic.verdict: An absolute beast of a soundbar: 11.1.4 with six up-firing drivers and detachable wireless rears
Aimed squarely at the Samsung Q990F

user_sentiment.summary: Owners single out the battery rears: they can be moved for a film and clipped back onto the bar afterwards, which suits a room where permanent rear speakers are not welcome.

pros: 11.1.4 with six up-firing drivers
Rears detach, charge on the bar and run on battery - no mains socket at the back of the room
Dual 8-inch wireless subwoofer
Three HDMI inputs
cons: The most expensive system here
Battery rears have to be remembered and recharged
Quoted peak power differs between JBL's page and the press release
cinema_verdict: The only four-piece set whose rears need nothing at all behind the sofa, and the only one with three HDMI inputs.
notes: No full lab review was available for the MK2 at the time of writing; the score is a synthesis of launch coverage and the MK1's reception.

critic.source: TechRadar (Arc Ultra vs Bose Smart Ultra)
critic.verdict: Reviewers favour the Arc for height effects; 14 drivers against the Bose's 9
9.1.4 with four height channels; Sound Motion bass avoids needing a separate subwoofer

user_sentiment.summary: Owners rate the height effects as the best available from a single bar and like that Sub 4 and Era 300 rears can be added later without cabling; the Sonos app is the usual complaint.

pros: 9.1.4 from one bar, four height channels
Sound Motion woofer gives real bass with no subwoofer box
Grows into a full surround set, all of it wireless
cons: No HDMI input at all - eARC only
A full set with Sub 4 and two Era 300s costs more than a Q990H
Depends on the Sonos app and account
cinema_verdict: The best single bar for height, and the best of this list for music; it needs two more purchases to match a four-piece Samsung set.
notes: Specs are taken from reviews and comparison tables rather than a Sonos spec sheet; the driver count (14) is consistent across them.

critic.verdict: A more compact Sonos Arc alternative; two upward-firing drivers among nine speakers
TrueSpace upmixing is the draw; the Arc is the better Atmos performer

user_sentiment.summary: Liked for dialogue clarity and for fitting under smaller TVs; owners who want bass end up buying a Bass Module.

pros: Two real up-firing dipole drivers in a small cabinet
TrueSpace upmixes non-Atmos content convincingly
Bass Module and surrounds are wireless when added
cons: Height effects rated below the Sonos Arc Ultra's
No DTS:X
No HDMI input
cinema_verdict: The compact true-Atmos bar: right for a small room, expensive once the Bass Module is added.
notes: Sources disagree on the channel count (3.0.2 in one comparison, nine speakers including two up-firing in another); recorded here as 5.0.2 on the driver count. Confidence low.

critic.verdict: A stunning Dolby Atmos soundbar with amazing bass for an all-in-one
Rock'n'roll styling, and the Atmos holds up
Styling meets movie magic

user_sentiment.summary: Bought as much for the look as the sound; owners report it works as a serious music system, helped by the RCA input for a turntable.

pros: 5.1.2 with two height channels and bass that reviewers rate without a subwoofer
RCA input for a turntable, plus Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3
HDMI input with 4K passthrough as well as eARC
cons: No rear speakers in the range at all
Heston Sub 200 is a separate purchase
Reviews disagree on driver count and power
cinema_verdict: The one to pick if the bar has to double as the hi-fi: real height channels, a phono-friendly input and no subwoofer needed to sound full.
notes: Scores well on the music profile because of the analogue input and streaming breadth; on the cinema profile it loses to four-piece sets for lack of rears.

critic.verdict: 5.1.2 with two up-firing drivers; 315 W RMS across eleven drivers
Manufacturer spec: six racetrack mid-woofers, three tweeters, two 2.75-inch up-firing units

user_sentiment.summary: Little owner feedback at the time of writing.

pros: Eleven drivers including two up-firing, in one bar
Matching wireless subwoofer and wireless surrounds available
Dolby Atmos and DTS:X
cons: Sub and surrounds both extra
Thin review coverage
One comparison table prints the layout as 9.0.2, which does not match the manufacturer
cinema_verdict: A credible single-bar Atmos system that expands wirelessly; priced against the Sonos Arc Ultra, which reviews rate higher.
notes: Confidence low: one consumer-group review and the manufacturer's own page.

critic.verdict: Convincing Dolby Atmos, powerful bass and an upbeat sound
System review: the bar takes up to two wireless subwoofers

user_sentiment.summary: Owners rate it as the most speaker-like bar at its price; the Flexus add-ons are the reason to choose it over a sealed system.

pros: Real up-firing height drivers at the bottom of the price range
Takes up to two wireless Flexus subwoofers and wireless surrounds
Reviewed well on bass for its size
cons: Nothing in the box but the bar
3.1.2 is the shallowest qualifying layout here
cinema_verdict: The cheapest route to drivers that actually fire at the ceiling, as long as you are willing to add the sub later.
notes: Street prices quoted between GBP 449 and USD 575 depending on the outlet.

critic.verdict: Sounds great, but is outshadowed by Samsung and Sonos in height reproduction
Manufacturer spec: nine channels, five upward-facing channels, separate subwoofer and two wireless rears

user_sentiment.summary: Owners pairing it with an LG TV value WOW Orchestra, which plays the TV's own speakers alongside the bar; the rears needing mains power is the common surprise.

pros: Five height channels, more than anything else on the list
Wireless subwoofer and wireless rears in the box
WOW Orchestra with LG TVs
cons: Height effects rated below Samsung's and Sonos'
Rears carry audio wirelessly but still need a socket
2024 model, so stock is thinning
cinema_verdict: The most height channels per euro when it is discounted, with the caveat that reviewers do not rate how it uses them.
notes: Weights from the Reviewed.com review: 12.5 lb bar, 9 lb rears, 22.1 lb subwoofer.
